newsitem.title: USA: GOP lawmakers in Ill. to push bond bill next month.
newsitem.headline: GOP lawmakers in Ill. to push bond bill next month.

text.p: Republicans in the Illinois House are planning to introduce a bill next month authorizing about $500 million in general obligation bond issuance, a spokesman for House Speaker Lee Daniels, R-Elmhurst, said Friday.
Mike Cys said Republicans will introduce the bill when the House returns to its fall veto session Dec. 3. The first week of the veto session ended Thursday.

The bill is expected to mirror previous proposals by Republican Gov. Jim Edgar, who was unsuccessful in getting the bonding bills passed over the last two years due to opposition by Democratic lawmakers. Those bills called for financing prison, higher education and other infrastructure projects with GO bonds.
However, Democrats in the Illinois House are not likely to support that level of bonding, according to Steve Brown, spokesman for House Minority Leader Michael Madigan, D-Chicago.

Brown said Democrats already introduced a bill authorizing the issuance of only $201 million of GO bonds for prison projects. That bill confirmed Madigan's statement in September that he would only support prison bonding in order to ease overcrowding and allow prison officials to begin deal with publicized problems of drug use and sex among prisoners.
While Republicans control the Senate, and until January the House, a three-fifths vote of the legislature is needed to approve bond authorization.

Another possible piece of legislation to head to lawmakers next month is a statewide advisory referendum on school funding. Cys said no bill has been drafted but that discussions were held on the referendum.

Earlier this year Edgar proposed a constitutional amendment requiring the state to pay at least 50 percent of education costs in exchange for lower local property taxes. The plan, however, failed to gain support in the legislature.
